calls.title: Legend + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The meeting focused on assessing GrowthBook's capabilities in comparison to SiteSpec and AB Tasty for enhancing front-end experimentation and feature flagging. Key challenges discussed included the over-reliance on SiteSpec for sports experiments, leading to distrust in its data, while the need for fast experimentation and robust server-side flagging was emphasized for upcoming React Native app releases. GrowthBook's features like Boolean flags, automatic rollback, and integration with Snowflake for data analysis were highlighted. The team also discussed visual editing capabilities, reusable design elements, and the importance of minimizing engineering efforts. With the evaluation phase concluding, they aim to finalize vendor selection by the end of the week, considering how GrowthBook aligns with existing tools and user feedback.

calls.title: Legend + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The team decided to proceed with Growthbook as the sole vendor, simplifying procurement and onboarding while moving through legal and pricing negotiations. The pricing structure includes an initial quote for 60 seats, split between full and read-only users, and despite being higher than competitors, it is justified by Growthbook's scalability and features. The target implementation timeline aims for a mid-year go-live for covers.com and casino.org, carefully aligned with the expiration of the current SiteSpec contract. Growthbook's integrated workflow is highlighted as a competitive edge, minimizing unexpected costs tied to traffic-based pricing models. User adoption discussions indicate that while engineers may be familiar with feature flagging, other teams will require additional support to ensure effective usage of the new tools.

calls.summary: The call discussed integrating GrowthBook with the client's Snowflake data warehouse, using Adobe Analytics as the event source, with pain points around the unexpected cost of GrowthBook's event forwarder and the need to handle data that updates only once daily. Key participants were Chris Sanders from GrowthBook and Net Management Ltd (Cato), Babak Tourani, and pilar.frontera from the client team. Next steps include the client's experimentation team identifying relevant events and metrics, configuring Snowflake as a read-only data source in GrowthBook, and potentially using the REST API to export results for custom dashboards.

calls.title: Legend + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The team discussed integrating GrowthBook with Snowflake by querying event and experiment data from their Adobe analytics setup, which avoids costly event forwarding options. The existing Adobe analytics pipeline stores relevant metrics in Snowflake, allowing for faster implementation without building a new API. Future plans include potentially exporting experiment results back into Snowflake for improved reporting. The team addressed data freshness by setting GrowthBook to poll Snowflake every 24 hours, ensuring minimal stale data querying. Optimizing query efficiency by pre-processing raw data into smaller tables was also emphasized. The roles of the experimentation and data engineering teams were defined, with the former responsible for identifying metrics and the latter for setting up and optimizing queries.
calls.keywords: GrowthBook, Snowflake, Experimentation Metrics, Data Integration, Event Forwarder, REST API
